articles.headline: OFAC Issues International Criminal Court Designation and General Licenses, Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, alongside new actions concerning the International Criminal Court (ICC) and Burma.
OFAC issued a designation related to the International Criminal Court and concurrently released associated General Licenses. This action follows ongoing U.S. policy regarding the ICC.
Additionally, OFAC removed a designation related to Burma, indicating a change in sanctions posture for a specific entity or individual previously targeted under the Burma sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new General License pertaining to Russia. This license outlines permissible transactions or activities that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia-related sanctions programs.

The issuance of General Licenses often aims to clarify the scope of sanctions, facilitate certain humanitarian efforts, or allow for specific types of commercial activities deemed not to undermine the overall sanctions objectives.
Entities and individuals engaging in Russia-related transactions are advised to review the specifics of this new General License to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Issues New Iran and Amended Russia General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter Iranian malign activities.
In conjunction with the new Iran-related designations, OFAC also issued a new General License specific to Iran, which may permit certain transactions or activities previously prohibited.

Furthermore, OFAC issued an amended Russia-related General License, indicating adjustments to existing authorizations for transactions involving Russia. Parties operating under previous Russia-related General Licenses should review the updated guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designations removals and updates, indicating changes to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and other sanctions lists.
In addition to these list adjustments, OFAC published an alert specifically related to Iran, likely providing guidance or warning about new evasion tactics or high-risk activities.
An amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) was also published, offering clarification on existing sanctions policies or compliance expectations for transactions involving Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism sanctions program. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist organizations or activities globally.
The designations aim to disrupt financial networks and limit the operational capabilities of terrorist groups by freezing assets and prohibiting transactions with the designated parties.
This move reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to combating terrorism financing and protecting the international financial system from illicit use.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Issues Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities and individuals involved in Iran-related activities and transnational criminal organizations.
These actions include updates to existing Iran-related designations and a new designation under the Transnational Criminal Organizations sanctions program, aiming to disrupt illicit networks.
OFAC also published an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question, providing further clarity and legal basis for the new measures and compliance expectations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations sanctions programs, targeting illicit actors globally.
Concurrently, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against specific entities or individuals in these areas.
These removals suggest a review of previous designations, potentially due to changed circumstances, successful remediation, or a shift in policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a broad set of new designations across multiple sanctions programs, including Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation.

These actions target a diverse range of illicit activities, aiming to disrupt drug trafficking, terrorist financing, Iranian destabilizing actions, and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
The comprehensive nature of these designations underscores the U.S. government's commitment to using sanctions as a tool to address various national security and foreign policy concerns.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, New Cuba Sanctions Regulations, and Amended FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has published significant regulatory amendments, including new Cuba Sanctions Regulations. These changes reflect a tightening of restrictions on transactions involving Cuba.
The new regulations implement Executive Order 14404 of May 1, 2026, which focuses on those responsible for repression in Cuba and threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy.
Accompanying these regulatory updates, OFAC also issued new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and a Cuba-related OFAC Alert, providing crucial guidance for compliance.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
